notes: POC objective: validate Dedicated capacity for production reranking at peak holiday-like load; get quantitative throughput guarantee and latency SLOs for contract.
Wanted: 99th percentile token latency < 200ms for single-turn reranking during 90th percentile load; steady-state throughput target = 1200 qps (inference requests), bursting to 2k qps for <15 min.
Representative workload: 70 candidates rerank per request (dense embeddings + cross-encoder scoring), average request size 1.2k tokens with 2x prefix caching on user session.
Hardware ask from customer: prefer H100-class nodes or equivalent; customer wants reserved pool sizing and headroom for 30% growth year-over-year.
Load test plan details: three phases - ramp (0->80% in 24h), peak soak (72h at target), resilience (chaos: node reboot, cold cache sweep, network variance).
Soak observations: batching aggressive (batch size 48) reduced token cost by ~28% but increased tail latency on cold starts; automatic prefix cache seeding cut p95 by ~35% in production-like replay.

SLA discussion notes: customer asks for financial credits tied to p95 latency and throughput floor. Proposed: 99.5% availability SLA, throughput floor guarantee (monthly) with pro-rated credits for underperformance. Legal wants example SLO language.
KMS and audit: customer requires HSM-backed key control for PII vectors and 3-year audit log retention; security asked for flow diagram for VPC peering and key lifecycle.
Quote from CTO: 'We need predictable token economics and a hard guarantee on throughput for Black Friday windows — can you give us planning numbers today?'

Infrastructure ask: recommended reserved capacity = 12 x H100-equivalent GPUs (with 2x burst capacity on on-demand) based on current workloads and 30% headroom; cost delta analyzed in attached pricing deck.
Open technical risk: model fallbacks during capacity saturation — customer requires automatic routing to quantized variant with fidelity delta <= 3% on rerank accuracy tests.

benchmark_summary: Baseline (no cache): 1200 qps synthetic replay -> p50 token latency 45ms, p95 token latency 340ms (cold cache windows drove tail)
With prefix caching + tuned batching: 1200 qps -> p50 38ms, p95 160ms, cost per 1k tokens down ~26%
Soak (72h) success criteria: no sustained CPU/GPU throttling, no SLA-breaking 30-minute outage, autoscaler held under 2x baseline nodes during bursts
Failure cases observed: synchronous cold cache flush during midnight job caused transient p95 spike to ~480ms for ~12 minutes — mitigation: background pre-warm and staggered eviction policy.
recommended_reserved_planning: Initial reserve: 12 GPUs (H100-equivalent) mapped into 3 pools: rerank-high, embeddings-batch, realtime-chat. Pool ratios 60/25/15.
Burst policy: allow 2x short-term burst using on-demand capacity for 15 minutes per hour across month; billing cushion defined in proposal.
Autoscale knobs: prefer node-level scale steps of 2 GPUs with ramp cooldown 10m, sustained CPU/GPU <70% target for scale-down.
Storage/cache sizing: KV cache target 1.5TB to hold active session caches; checkpoint retention 14 days for replay + evaluation.
sla_negotiation_notes: Customer wants hard throughput floor: 1,000 qps sustained with 2k qps 15-minute burst; Redwood proposed 90-day ramp to guarantee + credit schedule.
Latency SLO proposal: p95 token latency <200ms with monthly measurement window; credit tiers: 5% credit if missed 1-3 days, 15% if >3 days in month.
Availability: 99.5% per month with standard exception for scheduled maintenance (48h notice) and force majeure clauses.
Legal asks: example credit formulas, SLA termination clauses tied to repeated misses, data residency confirmation for EU users.
